label: early original-phase step within 2 steps after an l
explanation: Fires during the original (input) phase on the 1-2 steps right after the letter l was input, and only early in the sequence (t = 1..5; peak at t = 3, almost nothing at t >= 6). The token at the current step does not matter. Activation is largest when l is both one and two steps back (e.g. l l l x: about 1.0 of max at the step after the third l). It is weaker at t=1-2 (a single leading l gives about 0.15-0.2) and when l is only two steps back. Never fires in the copy phase and only rarely at the delimiter. Does not fire on l itself unless l was also the previous input. Misses are mostly weak activations (4-5% of mass) 3 steps after an l or with no recent l. Dev: P 0.91, R 0.76, F1 0.83, mass recall 0.95.

issues: One sentence in the explanation is wrong: 'It does not fire on an l itself unless the previous input was also l.' On dev, (phase==0)&(t<=5)&(rel_tok(-1)!=l)&(rel_tok(-2)==l)&(in_tok==l), i.e. the 'l x l' pattern, fires at precision 0.875 (n=1803). So the feature does fire on an l when there is an l two steps back. The predicate already covers this case and it holds only about 1% of the activation mass, so the label and predicate still stand. The sentence should say the current token does not matter, including when it is l.

The claim that it is weaker at t=5 is understated. At t=5, prediction accuracy drops to 0.69 when the previous token is l and 0.62 when l is only two steps back (dev), against 0.87-1.0 at t=1-4. Most of the predicate's false positives come from t=5. This is a gradual fade, not a separate class.

Misses are weak background activations: 3 steps after an l (precision 0.31 for that rule), or scattered activations around 0.01-0.05 of max with no recent l. Test coverage of the lowest activation quartile is 0.21, but misses hold only 4.8% of the mass. Adding 'l three steps back' for t<=4 gives dev F1 0.821 and for t<=3 gives 0.817, both slightly worse than the original's test F1 of 0.828, so no better predicate was found.

These claims check out: no firing in the copy phase (0 active steps); the delimiter carries 0.7% of the mass; t=0 is silent; t>=6 is almost silent (t=6 rate 0.005, t=7 has 50 steps); mass peaks at t=3 (0.356); 'l l l x' reaches 0.98-1.00 of max at the step after the third l (top examples); a single leading l gives 0.15-0.17 of max at t=1-2; the previous token being l gives precision 0.95 and two steps back gives 0.85, so l two steps back is weaker; the reported test scores reproduce (P 0.909, R 0.760, F1 0.828, mass recall 0.952).
